title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: VIV'S TOLL BOOTH
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Viv Rucker, a toll collector on the West Virginia Turnpike.
Viv talks to two thousand strangers a day. But she could not talk to her grandson, Eli.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE BIRTHDAY
segments.quote: Our doubts are traitors, and make us lose the good we oft might win, by fearing to attempt.
segments.author: William Shakespeare
lines: Eli was born deaf. At his fourth birthday, he signed fast with his mom, Tasha. Viv just waved, like he was a car in her lane.
Tasha handed her a flyer for a sign language night class. Viv said, Honey, I'm sixty-one.
Tasha quoted Shakespeare:
Our doubts are traitors, and make us lose the good we oft might win, by fearing to attempt.
Viv signed up that night.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE WRONG SIGN
segments.quote: Experience is the name every one gives to their mistakes.
segments.author: Oscar Wilde
lines: At Sunday dinner, she proudly signed: Grandma loves you. Eli fell off his chair laughing.
She had signed, Grandma is a bathroom. Then she remembered Oscar Wilde:
Experience is the name every one gives to their mistakes.
So she wrote Experience on a notebook, and filled it with mistakes.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: STIFF FINGERS
segments.quote: Patience serves as a protection against wrongs as clothes do against cold.
segments.author: Leonardo da Vinci
lines: By winter, her fingers were stiff from thirty years of making change. She wanted to quit.
Her husband Ray read her a line from Leonardo da Vinci:
Patience serves as a protection against wrongs as clothes do against cold.
Viv laughed. Then I'll wear my big coat.
She practiced on every break, signing thank you to every truck.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: SILLY SIGNS
segments.quote: We must laugh before we are happy, for fear of dying without having laughed at all.
segments.author: Jean de La Bruyère
lines: In January, a snowstorm kept Viv at Tasha's for three days.
Eli taught her his silly signs. One for Grandpa's snoring. One for Grandma's big earrings.
She remembered the French writer La Bruyère:
We must laugh before we are happy, for fear of dying without having laughed at all.
They laughed until the dog barked, and she stopped being scared.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: RAY TRIES
segments.quote: Correction does much, but encouragement does more.
segments.author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
lines: Then Ray tried. He signed pass the gravy like he was swatting flies.
Viv wanted to fix every swat. Then she thought of Goethe:
Correction does much, but encouragement does more.
So she cheered. By spring, Ray could sign pass the gravy. He has not stopped since.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: NO WORDS NEEDED
segments.quote: The best and most beautiful things in the world cannot be seen nor even touched, but just felt in the heart.
segments.author: Helen Keller
lines: On his fifth birthday, Eli signed slowly: Grandma, I love you. She signed it back. No words needed.
She thought of Helen Keller, who wrote this in a letter:
The best and most beautiful things in the world cannot be seen nor even touched, but just felt in the heart.
Now her toll booth window has a card: I sign. Deaf truckers honk and wave.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Start anyway. Keep your mistakes. Bundle up. Laugh first. Cheer people on. Feel it in your heart.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Start anyway. Keep your mistakes. Bundle up. Laugh first. Cheer people on. Feel it in your heart.
Me? I learned one sign this week. It means more cake.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
